data.headword: hǧəmle/hoǧəm l-raġloṯe d- 'jemandem zu Füßen stürzen (bittend)'
data.turoyo: Nafəq aṯi hǧəmle lraġloṯe d Oṣman Aġá, nšəqle raġloṯe, nšəqle iḏoṯe, nšəqle foṯe, omar, ‘Kobaʕno dlo+quṭlatli, lo+ṭorat an+nišayḏi bu+ʕulmo’.
data.translation: He got out, he flung himself at the feet of Oṣman Aġá, he kissed his feet, he kissed his hands, he kissed his face, he says, ‘I want you not to kill me, do not abandon my wives to the world!’
data.ref: MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/52

rationale: One clear supplication context: feet goal, kissing and a plea. Searched raġloṯ in the glossary: no matching hǧm collocation. Its conventionality remains open.

summary: The supplied 114 records all concern stem I. The ordinary attack/rush meaning is sufficient; repeated tokens in JTM and MAC remain separate decisions, not independent events.

Valency: ʕal- and l- targets alternate with bound target expressions, including the singular/plural-agent contrast hǧə́mlelan / hǧə́mmallan (MAC NI MAR YUHANEN/10), reciprocal ləḥḏoḏe (MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/11), and l rišayna (JTM 3.1/23). These are active constructions, not Detransitive forms.

Preterit-wa at MAC Murder in Kfarze, Interview with Numan/56 and Infectum-wa at MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/111 are overt. A nocturnal setting alone does not prove habituality, and -wa alone does not establish a specific anteriority relation.
The Arabic-derived root behaves as an inflected lexical verb. sym huǧum is mentioned at 112/407 but is not supplied as an occurrence here; no example or idiom is reconstructed from that allusion.
The source’s ḥ spellings at MAC Murder in Kfarze concern attack and are preserved; they do not justify changing this root to a distinct fitting-into-a-room verb.

Nominal hǧomo has two supplied contexts; the topic construction and its contrast with finite həǧmo support Nomen Actionis. Agentive haǧomo at 52/113 is documented here without imposing Part act. status.

No further routine examples are added to the five-example Preterit and Infectum cells. The chosen suffixed-target pair supplies a clear contrast; repeated assaults and alternative body-part targets add no separate sense.
Round 1 already supplies Preterit-wa, Infectum-wa and Nomen Actionis. Reader new-box claims based on the original glossary are not repeated.
Overtly daily attack at 2.3/326 and counterfactual Gədhəǧmiwo at 2.4/715 show distinct discourse functions of Infectum-wa; a night setting alone does not decide aspect.
hǧəmme recurs with plural agents, while hǧəmle occurs with a collective u ʕamo. Avoid deriving number solely from the apparent -me ending.
Agentive Hǧim at 1.3/56 does not by itself prove a Detransitive section. The identical reduced həǧmiwo elsewhere has ordinary Infectum-wa uses.
haǧəm at 2.5/1220 provisionally supplies a finite Preterit Intransitive form in a past-event question; confirmation of the borrowing’s morphology remains necessary.
Is haǧomo at 52/113 a lexical agent noun or a member of a productive Part act. paradigm? Is hǧomo also licensed in productive Infinitiv constructions?
How is kalkó segmented in MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/116? Does independent grammatical evidence license a ko-Preterit analysis here?
Does hǧámmule at MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/45 narrate an attack or repeat an Imperativ with a target suffix?
Is rushing to someone’s feet a conventional supplication collocation beyond the single attestation at MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/52?
At JTM 3.1/25, does laṣ ṣuroye correct the agent or mark a target? Do not assign the sides from the translation alone.
Confirm segmentation of hǧəmanne / hǧəmlanne and whether non-hostile l-goals admit the same bound target series as assaults.
Jan 1.3/56: is Hǧim a finite qaṭəl-like borrowing, a deponent Detransitive form, or an irregular spelling? Its agent is the attacking qaymaqam. No new Detransitive is published from the shape alone.
